text: Alright, let's start putting together this advanced lithium-ion battery pack assembly for the electric vehicle prototype. First, the individual 18650 cells that arrived this morning were inspected by Sarah using the high-precision digital multimeter from our premium testing kit. Each cell measures exactly 65 millimeters in length and weighs about 48 grams. Sarah and Mike will work together on this assembly while I heat up the ultrasonic welding station to 250 degrees Celsius. The battery management system board, which was manufactured last week in our facility, needs to be hooked up to the main cell array. Mike is setting up the spot welding equipment on the main workbench while Sarah takes apart the protective packaging from each battery cell. The nickel strips that we'll use for connections were cut by the fabrication team yesterday to precise 2.5 millimeter widths. Next, Sarah puts together the first module of six cells in series, and after that, she connects them using the pre-cut nickel strips. The temperature monitoring sensors, which cost us nearly 200 dollars each, get installed between every third cell group. Then Mike turns on the automated testing sequence that checks each connection for proper resistance - we're looking for readings under 5 milliohms. The completed first module that Sarah assembled weighs approximately 290 grams total. Before we move on, the voltage across the entire pack was measured by Mike at exactly 22.2 volts using our calibrated Fluke multimeter. Finally, we'll wrap up by installing the protective housing and running a full 30-minute charge cycle test.
